p: I think myself happy: To have a skilful judge is a great and singular gift of God.
My manner of life from my: Paul divides the history of his life into two times: for the first he calls his adversaries as witnesses: for the latter, the fathers and Prophets.
knew me from: That I was, and where, and how I lived.
the beginning: That my parents were Pharisees.
most straitest sect of our religion: The sect of the Pharisees was the most exquisite amongst all the sects of the Jews, for it was better than all the rest.
And now I stand and am: There are three chief and principal witnesses of true doctrine: God, the true fathers, and the consent of the true Church of God.
Why should it be thought a: He proves the resurrection of the dead, first by the power of God, then by the resurrection of Christ, of which he is a sufficient witness.
my voice against them: I consented to and allowed their actions: for he was not a judge.
compelled them to blaspheme: By extreme punishment.
To open their eyes: The end of the Gospel is to save those who are brought to the knowledge of Christ, and are justified and sanctified in him, being laid hold on by faith.
Whereupon: Paul alleges God to be author of the office of his apostleship, and that God's grace is a witness.
Having therefore obtained help of God: Christ is the end of the Law and the Prophets.
small and great: To everyone.
suffer: That Christ would not be such a king as the Jews dreamed of, but one appointed to bear our miseries, and the punishment of our sins.
first that should rise from the: The first of those who are raised from the dead.

light unto the people: Life, yea and that a most blessed life which will be endless: and this is set against darkness, which almost in all languages sometimes signifies death, and sometimes misery and calamity.
And as he thus spake for: The wisdom of God is madness to fools, yet nonetheless we must boldly confirm the truth.
corner: Secretly and privately.
King Agrippa: Paul, as it were forgetting that he stood a prisoner to defend his cause, does not forget the office of his apostleship.
I would to God: I would to God that not only almost, but thoroughly and altogether, both you and all that hear me this day, might be made as I am, only except for my bonds.
And when he had thus spoken: Paul is solemnly acquitted, and yet not dismissed.
